items.title: What does engine fitting cost in the UK?
items.description: Engine fitting costs typically range from £800 to £2,500 depending on vehicle complexity, engine type, and your location. Most standard front-wheel-drive vehicles cost £800-£1,500 to fit, while 4WD, performance, and prestige vehicles cost £1,500-£2,500+ .

items.title: Common questions about engine fitting costs

blocks.question: How much does engine fitting cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Engine fitting costs typically range from £800 to £2,500 depending on vehicle complexity, engine type, and your location. Standard front-wheel-drive vehicles cost £800-£1,500; 4WD and performance vehicles cost £1,500-£2,500+. Labour accounts for 40-60% of total engine replacement expenses.

blocks.question: How long does engine fitting take? +
blocks.answer: Typical fitting time is 2-5 days. Standard 4-cylinder FWD vehicles take 2-3 days. V8 4WD vehicles take 4-5 days. Complex or rare engines may take longer. The timeline depends on vehicle complexity, parts availability, and the garage's workload.

blocks.question: What's included in engine fitting? +
blocks.answer: Removal of old engine, fitting of customer engine, transfer of ancillaries, new consumables (oil, coolant, filters), basic testing (compression, oil pressure), and disposal of old unit. Always check the written quote for exact inclusions.

blocks.question: What's NOT included in engine fitting? +
blocks.answer: Engine supply (you provide your own engine), warranty on your customer-supplied engine, clutch/DMF, water pump, timing components, air-con regas, unforeseen repairs, and hire car. Your engine is not warranted - you accept the risk.

blocks.question: What's the labour rate for engine fitting in the UK? +
blocks.answer: The average labour rate in the UK is currently £68.51 per hour [THIRD-PARTY]. Independent specialists charge £55-£160/hour (regional variation). Main dealers charge £90-£220/hour (regional variation). Independent specialists are typically 40-60% cheaper than main dealers.

blocks.question: Should I use an independent specialist or a main dealer? +
blocks.answer: For most customers, an independent specialist offers the best balance of cost and quality. Main dealers are significantly more expensive (40-60% higher) but offer manufacturer training and specialist tools. Use a main dealer if your vehicle is under warranty or you're claiming on insurance.

blocks.question: Can I supply my own engine and have it fitted? +
blocks.answer: Yes. Many garages are happy to fit customer-supplied engines. However, the garage does NOT warranty your engine - you accept the risk. Ask the garage to inspect your engine before fitting. Get everything in writing.

blocks.question: What happens if my customer-supplied engine is faulty? +
blocks.answer: If you supply your own engine and it's faulty, the garage is not responsible. You'll pay for removal and refitting again. Ask the garage to inspect the engine before fitting to verify its condition. This may cost extra but could save you thousands.

blocks.question: How long does a fitted engine take to run in? +
blocks.answer: Most engines require a run-in period of 500-1,000 miles. Avoid heavy acceleration, high revs, and towing during this period. Vary the engine speed (don't sit at the same speed on motorways). Follow the garage's specific run-in instructions.

blocks.question: Do I need to tell my insurer about the new engine? +
blocks.answer: Yes. Any major mechanical change, including engine replacement, must be declared to your insurer. The new engine code and number should be recorded on your V5C (logbook) and insurance policy. Failure to do so could invalidate your insurance.

blocks.question: What's the difference between engine fitting and engine replacement? +
blocks.answer: Engine replacement typically includes supply of a new or reconditioned engine plus fitting. Engine fitting is labour-only - you supply the engine and the garage fits it. If you've already sourced your own engine, you need engine fitting.

blocks.question: Can I watch the engine being fitted? +
blocks.answer: Some garages allow customers to observe the work, others don't for insurance and safety reasons. Ask the garage about their policy. Trusted garages will provide photos and updates during the process.

blocks.question: What testing is included in engine fitting? +
blocks.answer: Basic testing is typically included: compression test, oil pressure test, visual inspection for leaks, and a short test drive. Comprehensive dyno testing is usually extra (£100-£300) and only available at some garages.

blocks.question: Should I replace ancillaries during engine fitting? +
blocks.answer: If your alternator, starter, injectors, turbo, or other ancillaries are worn, it's sensible to replace them while the engine is out. The labour cost to replace them later is much higher. Ask the garage to inspect your ancillaries and advise.
